documents.title: History and Physical - Admission, COPD Exacerbation
lines: HPI:
66 yo M with known severe COPD presents to ED at 01:20 with 3 days of worsening dyspnea, cough, and thick yellow sputum.
Symptoms began after a head cold in the household; used his home rescue inhaler q2h at home over the last 24h with minimal relief.
On arrival unable to complete sentences. Denies chest pain, fever at home, hemoptysis, leg swelling, or orthopnea.
No sick contacts with known influenza. No recent travel. No prior intubation. Two prior admissions for the same in the past 2 yrs.
Triage vitals: SpO2 84% on room air, HR 118, BP 158/88, RR 32, temp 37.1.
ED Course:
Nasal cannula titrated up; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
Magnesium 2 g IV given at 02:45. Azithromycin 500 mg IV started at 02:50.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Placed on BiPAP 14/6 at 03:30 for work of breathing.
CXR portable: hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation, no pneumothorax, no effusion.
PMH:
COPD, GOLD 3 by prior PFTs (FEV1 41% predicted)
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension
Hyperlipidemia
Former smoker, 45 pack-yr, quit 4 yrs ago
Home Meds:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID
Lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
Allergies: sulfa (rash)
Social: lives with wife, 1 flight of stairs to bedroom, daughter nearby. No alcohol. No illicit drugs.
Physical Exam:
General: ill appearing, anxious, sitting upright at edge of bed.
Resp: Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Diffuse expiratory wheeze bilaterally with prolonged expiratory phase; poor air movement at bases.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, no JVD, no peripheral edema.
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Neuro: awake, follows commands, no asterixis, no focal deficit.
Skin: warm, dry, no cyanosis.
Labs:
WBC 13.6, Hgb 14.9, Plt 244
Glucose 186 on admission
Troponin <0.01 x1, BNP 62
Influenza A/B PCR negative, resp viral panel pending
Assessment/Plan:
66 yo M with severe COPD, acute exacerbation with acute on chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure, likely viral/bacterial trigger.
1. Resp failure: continue BiPAP 14/6, wean to NC as tolerated targeting SpO2 88-92%. Repeat ABG in 4h. ICU-level monitoring in step-down.
2. Obstruction: albuterol-ipratropium neb q4h scheduled, q2h prn between.
3. Inflammation: IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours.
4. Infection: azithromycin IV, sputum cx sent, procalcitonin pending.
5. DM: hold metformin, insulin sliding scale, q6h glucose checks - anticipate steroid hyperglycemia.
6. HTN: hold lisinopril while volume/BP labile, resume when stable.
7. VTE ppx: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily.
8. Smoking cessation reinforced. RT and pulmonary hygiene at bedside.
Discussed with wife at bedside at 04:10. Full code.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: Subjective:
Pt reports breathing better than on arrival. Tolerated mask overnight, slept in 2h blocks. Cough still productive, sputum lighter in color.
Overnight events: remained on BiPAP continuously for 9 hours, then transitioned to 3L NC at 12:30 per RT. No arrhythmia, no hypotension.
Glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale; 8 units regular given at 06:00.
Vitals: T 36.9, HR 96, BP 142/80, RR 22, SpO2 91% on 3L NC.
I/O 1200/1450. Weight stable.
Exam:
Gen: more comfortable, conversing in full sentences now.
Resp: mild accessory muscle use only, no tripoding. Expiratory wheeze still audible bilaterally, air movement improved.
CV: RRR, no murmur, no edema.
Neuro: alert, oriented, no asterixis.
Labs this AM:
WBC 11.2, Hgb 14.4, Plt 230
Repeat ABG at 08:00: pH 7.36, PaCO2 52, PaO2 71 on 3L
Sputum cx: mixed respiratory flora, no predominant organism. Procalcitonin 0.14.
Assessment/Plan:
COPD exacerbation with hypercapnic respiratory failure, improving on HD2.
1. Continue albuterol-ipratropium neb q4h; wean to MDI with spacer this afternoon if stable.
2. Continue methylprednisolone 40 mg IV q8h; plan transition to prednisone 40 mg PO daily when weaned off NIV support.
3. O2: target SpO2 88-92%, wean NC as tolerated. Plan nocturnal NIV tonight given overnight hypercapnia.
4. Steroid hyperglycemia: continue insulin sliding scale, q4h checks, add 4 units lispro with meals if >250 persists.
5. Abx: narrow, continue azithromycin, day 2 of 5.
6. Mobilize with PT, incentive spirometry q1h while awake.
7. Resume lisinopril today - BP trending up.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: Interval note, 16:20.
Subjective:
Pt ambulated to hallway and back with RN, ~100 ft, mild dyspnea, recovered in 2 min. Denies chest pain or lightheadedness.
Asked about going home; educated that he will need overnight support tonight first.
Vitals at 16:00: HR 88, BP 136/78, RR 18, SpO2 92% on 2L NC, SpO2 90% on RA seated.
Ambulation check: SpO2 nadir 88% on 2L, recovered to 92% after 1 min rest.
Glucose 244 at 12:00, 188 at 16:00 - 4 units lispro given at lunch.
Exam:
Resp: no accessory muscle use at rest. Scattered end-expiratory wheeze, much improved air entry.
CV: RRR. Abd soft. Extremities without edema.
Plan updates:
1. Converted to albuterol-ipratropium MDI 2 puffs q4h with spacer at 15:00; neb q4h prn breakthrough. Technique observed and adequate.
2. BiPAP 14/6 to be resumed nocturnally on night 2 starting 22:00; RT notified.
3. Steroid: last IV dose at 16:00, then prednisone 40 mg PO daily starting tomorrow AM.
4. Continue insulin sliding scale, q4h glucose; hold metformin until discharge.
5. Continue azithromycin, day 2 of 5.
6. If tolerates night on NIV with AM pCO2 <50 and stable sat on room air/low-flow, anticipate discharge HD3.
7. Home inhaler regimen reviewed with wife by phone at 15:45; she will bring device list in AM.
8. Enoxaparin ppx continued. No new issues. Will reassess in AM.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD3
lines: Discharge Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of COPD with acute on chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure.
Secondary: type 2 diabetes with steroid-induced hyperglycemia, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
Hospital Course:
66 yo M with GOLD 3 COPD admitted overnight HD1 with 3 days of worsening dyspnea and purulent sputum.
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Placed on BiPAP 14/6 at 03:30 for work of breathing; remained on BiPAP continuously for 9 hours, then nocturnally on night 2.
CXR showed hyperinflation without consolidation. Influenza PCR negative. Sputum cx mixed flora. Procalcitonin 0.14.
Treated with IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours, azithromycin, scheduled bronchodilators, and pulmonary hygiene.
Glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale; metformin held during admission.
By HD2 afternoon he was on 2L NC, ambulating 100 ft, and converted to MDI with spacer.
HD3 AM: ABG pH 7.40, PaCO2 45, PaO2 78 on room air. SpO2 93% on RA at rest, 90% with ambulation, no accessory muscle use.
Steroid transitioned to prednisone 40 mg PO daily. Glucose 162 at 06:00, 148 at 11:00.
Stable for discharge HD3 at 14:40.
Discharge Exam:
Comfortable, full sentences, RR 16, HR 84, BP 130/76, SpO2 93% room air. Faint expiratory wheeze only at bases.
Discharge Medications:
Prednisone 40 mg PO daily x3 more days, then stop
Azithromycin 250 mg PO daily to complete 5-day course
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily - resume
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID - resume
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID - resume
Lisinopril 20 mg PO daily, atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
Instructions:
Check fingersticks BID while on prednisone; call if consistently >300.
Return for increased sputum, fever, worsening breathlessness at rest, or confusion.
Inhaler and spacer technique demonstrated by pt to RN prior to discharge.
Continue smoking abstinence; pulmonary rehab referral placed.
Follow-up:
Pulmonary clinic in 7 to 10 days with repeat spirometry when stable.
Primary care in 1 week for glucose and BP recheck.
Condition at discharge: stable, home with wife.
